Mohsin vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023
Author: Deepak Verma
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 78 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 19221 of 2022 Applicant :- Mohsin Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 19221 of 2022

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- S.M.Ayaz Ali,Rajesh Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
Counter affidavit filed today on behalf of State, is taken on record.
Heard Sri Bilal Hasan, Advocate, holding brief of Sri S.M.Ayaz, learned counsel for the applicant,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant Mohsin with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.06 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420 I.P.C., P.S. Ramgarh, District Firozabad during pendency of the trial.
It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that initially applicant was released on bail in Case Crime No.23 of 2006 under section 307 I.P.C. Thereafter, he was not participated in court proceedings, therefore, non-bailable warrant was issued and applicant was arrested.
Applicant was released on bail on 22.02.2022 in Case Crime No.23 of 2006 under section 307 I.P.C.

In compliance Mohsin vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52950726/
1 of non-bailable warrant issued, applicant was arrested with forged Aadhar card and implicated in the present case.

sentences.text: There is no prospect of trial of the present case being concluded in near future due to heavy dockets.
The applicant is not a previous convict.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 06.01.2022 and in case he is enlarged on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India, Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another, passed in S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Let the applicant, Mohsin, who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/ pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
2. The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
3. The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

Order Date :- 20.1.2023/SKD  Mohsin vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52950726/
